subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by landing the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal first, or should maintainers require explicit WebChat/heartbeat/channel-level retry parity before treating the bug as fixed?
rationale: Current source proves both a shared conflict throw and surface-specific terminalization paths, but choosing shared self-heal versus per-surface retry changes the permanent owner boundary for session lifecycle recovery.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest WebChat and heartbeat conflict cases before adding surface-specific retry loops.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Queue a separate repair that classifies reply-session-init conflicts as retryable for WebChat and heartbeat-style inbound paths regardless of the shared PR.

options.title: Ask For Live Surface Proof
options.body: Keep this issue open while requesting current-main live reproduction for the exact WebChat or heartbeat path before choosing the repair layer.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest WebChat and heartbeat conflict cases before adding surface-specific retry loops.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest verified history on the guarded reply-session initialization boundary where the shared recovery decision sits.
